input.title: Add toFahrenheit export to src/temperature.js
input.plan:
## Problem

`npm test` fails before any test runs. `node --test` loads `test/temperature.test.mjs`, whose line 4 is:

```js
import { toCelsius, toFahrenheit } from '../src/temperature.js';
```

`src/temperature.js` only exports `toCelsius`, so the module fails to instantiate with:

```
SyntaxError: The requested module '../src/temperature.js' does not provide an export named 'toFahrenheit'
```

This is a module-resolution error, not an assertion failure — the whole test file aborts.

## Change

**File: `src/temperature.js`** (the only file that changes — no test edits, no new files, no dependency changes)

Add a `toFahrenheit` export below the existing `toCelsius`, mirroring its style (JSDoc comment noting the direction and one-decimal rounding):

```js
/** Celsius -> Fahrenheit, rounded to one decimal. */
export function toFahrenheit(c) {
  return Math.round((c * 9) / 5 + 32) * 10) / 10;
}
```

(The exact form written will be `Math.round(((c * 9) / 5 + 32) * 10) / 10` — grouped the same way as the existing `toCelsius` body.)

### Why round to one decimal

The test file's third case is the binding constraint:

```js
for (const f of [-40, 68, 98.6]) {
  assert.equal(toFahrenheit(toCelsius(f)), f);
}
```

`assert.equal` from `node:assert/strict` is a strict `===` with no tolerance, and `toCelsius` **already rounds to one decimal**, so `toFahrenheit` receives a rounded Celsius value and must return the original Fahrenheit exactly. Rounding the output to one decimal, exactly as `toCelsius` does, makes the round-trip exact for every test input because each input Fahrenheit value has at most one decimal place — this holds even if the unrounded expression lands a fraction of an ulp off, which is the failure mode that would otherwise make this test flaky.

The other cases are satisfied directly: `toFahrenheit(0) === 32` and `toFahrenheit(100) === 212`.

## Order of steps

1. Add the `toFahrenheit` function to `src/temperature.js` after `toCelsius`.
2. Run `npm test` and confirm all 3 tests pass.

## Verification

`npm test` (i.e. `node --test`), which should report `pass 3` / `fail 0` and exit 0, replacing the current `fail 1` with the `SyntaxError`. This single command exercises both the import fix and all three behavioral assertions, including the strict round-trip case.
